_bridge: tests/security/scan-fidelity.test.mjs runs the REAL scanner over that HTML and deep-compares this file to its output. Edit one and the other goes red.
_why: bench-apply.mjs's board resolver THREW for `--board lever`, so the one board in the corpus with a NATIVE <select> — options already in the DOM, where probing is pure waste — could not be measured against the two where probing is unavoidable. Phase 0.10.
_finding_g1: READ THIS BEFORE TRUSTING g1. Until 2026-08-18 the sponsorship question's group label was "Yes" — the first radio's own option text — because Lever puts the question in a <div class="application-label"> SIBLING of the <ul>, and scan-page.js's wrapping-<label> tier won before the four-ancestor class walk could reach it. The scanner's group-question pass (the block after the button-pair helpers in scan-page.js) now recognises a multi-option group whose `l` is one of its own options and takes the question from the options' container instead — the same walk and bounds the button-pair detector uses — so `l` is the question a human sees and `labelWhy` says so ("label source is group question"). The trailing required glyph ("✱") is dropped by questionIn(), which keeps the text up to the last "?". Consumer-level assertions: tests/security/board-fidelity.test.mjs (the former FINDING, now the fix) and tests/apply/scan-page.test.mjs.
_g2_consent: The privacy-policy tickbox is a single-option checkbox GROUP (g2) with `labelExact`. It is the shape rule 6 defers on regardless of topic — a checkbox carries assent, not a value.
_k_order: No combos on this page, so the stamp order IS reading order (f1..f10) and the two groups g1/g2 are minted after the inputs they contain. Contrast greenhouse-step1 and ashby-step1, where a combo takes f1.
